subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` config writes warn or fail for unknown and pattern-like entries, and how should plugin/custom command IDs be treated?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent behavior changes a security-sensitive config boundary where fail-closed validation can break valid custom/plugin command policy.

options.title: Warn first for unknown entries
options.body: Emit a write-time warning with audit-style suggestions while still allowing custom and plugin command IDs to be stored.

options.title: Fail closed for invalid built-ins
options.body: Reject unknown or pattern-like entries only after defining a plugin-aware known-command vocabulary and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Keep audit-only detection
options.body: Leave config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to report ineffective denylist entries later.

recommendation.title: Warn first for unknown entries
recommendation.body: Emit a write-time warning with audit-style suggestions while still allowing custom and plugin command IDs to be stored.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history signal for both the node command policy and the security audit boundary affected by this decision.
